headline: KOSPI slides 3.6% on AI-funding fears and a strong 30Y auction pulls the long end lower: 10Y −3.3bp to 4.001%, 30Y −4.2bp, while a 2.8% CPI leaves the 1–3Y anchored
summary: KTBs bull-flattened as stocks gave back Monday's rebound and more. The long end led: 30Y −4.2bp to 4.089%, 50Y −4.0bp to 4.115% and 10Y −3.3bp to 4.001%, while the 3Y barely moved (−0.4bp to 3.736%) and the 1Y held at 3.584%, so 3s10s flattened to 26.5bp, about a basis point off its 1-year low. October CPI at 2.8% was in line to slightly soft but not enough to price out a November hike: MSB 91-day stayed at 3.185% and CD 91-day rose another 1bp to 3.35%, a new 1-year high. KDB held about 28bp over KTB at 1–3Y, AAA bank debentures narrowed 2bp to 42bp over the 1Y KTB, and AA- 3Y was 69bp over, all still wide against their 1-year averages.
drivers: KOSPI fell 3.59% to 5,648.79 (KOSDAQ −4.1%) as big US tech funding plans revived doubts about AI returns; foreigners sold KRW 1.53tn of KOSPI stock, their third straight day, and institutions KRW 0.51tn. The bid went to duration, not the front end: 20–50Y fell 3.5–4.2bp, more than undoing Monday's payback.

MOEF sold KRW 2tn of 30Y KTBs at 4.070% with a 197% bid-to-cover, 1–2bp through where the 30Y traded during the auction window, on insurer and other end-user demand. That anchored the ultra-long rally and kept 10s30s near 9bp.

The US 10Y par yield fell 3bp to 4.91% on Monday as oil dropped 7% on US–Iran talk hopes, despite a firm 55.5 ISM. At the 1-year daily beta of 0.46 that implied a 1.4bp KTB rally; the 10Y fell 3.3bp, so about 1.9bp was local (equity-driven). The KTB–UST 10Y gap stayed near −91bp, the 4th percentile of the year. On our basket valuation 10Y futures fair value rose 35 ticks to 108.19 and 3Y 2 ticks to 103.63; we did not find settle prices in the wraps, so no basis read today.

October CPI rose 2.8% y/y (Reuters poll 2.85%, prior 2.9%) and 0.2% m/m (f 0.3%), with core steady at 2.8%. The finance ministry estimates the fuel price cap shaved 0.8pp off headline, and processed food and dining-out prices accelerated, so the 2Y eased only 1.8bp and the 1Y and 3Y hardly moved.
data: In line to a touch soft. Without the fuel price cap headline would be about 3.6%, so it does not rule out a November 26 hike; front end steady.
Strong end-user demand; long-end supportive despite issuance up KRW 0.2tn on the month.
Record-type trade strength underpins the won and the BOK's hawkish lean; markets are trading AI-capex doubts instead.
Fastest output gain since 2011 on chips and autos; activity data keep hike pricing in the 1–2Y.
Large beat on chip capex and government spending; private consumption fell 0.2%.
Hold at 3.00%, unanimous (after +25bp in July and August)
Guided to staying restrictive; a November 26 hike to 3.25% remains the base case in the front end.
Pending; a large surplus is expected
Mainly a won story; little direct KTB impact.
view: Today confirmed that Monday was a pause: KOSPI resumed its slide, foreigners kept selling stocks, and the bond-rally signal firmed to +1.71 with all four inputs except the small ETF part pointing to bonds. Over four weeks about −21bp of the 10Y's −39bp came from US Treasuries at a weekly beta of 0.58 and −18bp was Korea's own equity-to-bond rotation, and today split roughly 40/60 global/local. With CPI not soft enough to remove a November hike, I expect the 10Y to hold 3.92–4.10% over the next two weeks, with rallies led by the long end; I would buy only on a back-up toward 4.10%. The 3s10s steepener is 2.8bp against and near its stop as insurers chase 30Y supply, so I keep it on with the 25bp stop unchanged but would not add; the 50Y-over-30Y switch and KDB overweight stay. The rotation view is best expressed against Treasuries: hedged with 0.58 × US 10Y, the live signal's rally calls hit 66% and sell-off calls 69% (48% and 57% outright), with a Sharpe of 1.23 against 0.93. Bank paper and corporates still wait for CP–CD (47bp) to come off.

buckets.name: KTB 1–2Y front end
buckets.why: The 2Y fell 1.8bp to 3.701% (76th percentile of its 1-year range, average 3.36%) and the 1Y held at 3.584% (87th). CPI at 2.8% was not soft enough to remove a November hike: MSB 91-day is at 3.185%, 99th percentile, and 2s3s steepened 1.4bp to 3.5bp, still the 3rd percentile.
buckets.call: No trigger hit (CPI came at 2.8%, not below). Add 2Y above 3.80%; fade rallies below 3.62%.

buckets.name: 3s10s curve
buckets.why: 3s10s flattened 2.9bp to 26.5bp, the 1st percentile of the year (average 40bp, low 26.2bp), as equity weakness and the strong 30Y auction pulled the long end down while hike pricing pinned the 3Y. Our steepener from 29.3bp is 2.8bp against and 1.5bp from its stop. One 10Y future carries about 3.0 times the DV01 of a 3Y (KRW 86k vs 29k per bp).
buckets.call: Keep the 3s10s steepener (buy 3 × 3Y, sell 1 × 10Y futures) from 29bp; target 36bp, stop 25bp. Open, 2.8bp against.

buckets.name: KTB 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 4.001% is at the 52nd percentile of a 3.08–4.60% range, 39bp lower over four weeks. Less than half of today's −3.3bp came from Treasuries (implied −1.4bp at a 0.46 beta), and the KTB–UST gap of −91bp (4th percentile) says Korea has already outperformed a lot.
buckets.call: Buy zone 4.10–4.15% not reached; keep it with a stop at 4.25%. Don't chase below 4.00%.

buckets.name: Ultra-long 30–50Y
buckets.why: 30s50s is +2.6bp, the 96th percentile of the year (average −9.7bp); the switch from +2.5bp is flat as both legs rallied about 4bp after the 30Y auction cleared through the market. Off-the-run 2042 and 2054 KTBs trade 8–9bp cheap to the fitted curve, while the 2028 3Y futures basket bond is about 5bp rich.
buckets.call: Keep the 30Y into 50Y switch at +2.5bp; target −3bp, stop +6bp. Open, flat.

buckets.name: KDB 1–3Y vs KTB
buckets.why: The KDB fit (15 trades) puts KDB 28bp over KTB at 1–3Y; at 3Y that is the 90th percentile against a 19bp average, about 2bp wider than our entry. KOFIA's own 1Y KDB quote is 34bp over (95th percentile, average 23bp). KEXIM prices similarly, but its fit uses only 5 trades, so treat it as low confidence.
buckets.call: Hold the overweight from ~26bp; take profit at 20bp, cut above 35bp. Open, about 2bp against.

buckets.name: AAA bank debentures and money market
buckets.why: AAA bank paper (46-trade fit) narrowed 1.9bp to 42bp over the 1Y KTB, still the 94th percentile (average 30bp). CD 91-day rose to 3.35% and CP to 3.82%, both 1-year highs, with CP–CD at 47bp (94th percentile, average 27bp). IBK 1Y at 38bp over is a 1-year wide.
buckets.call: No change: prefer KDB over bank debentures; revisit bank paper once CP–CD falls below 35bp.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AA- 3Y)
buckets.why: AA- 3Y is 69bp over the KTB (80th percentile, average 60bp) and KEPCO 3Y 44bp over (99th percentile). Spreads were steady through a 3.6% equity fall, which is resilient, but with KOSPI back under 5,700 there is no turn to buy into yet.
buckets.call: Add AA- only above 75bp or once KOSPI holds a rebound for a week; no trigger hit.

watch: Next: US midterm elections (Tue Nov 3, results Wed in Asia), the US quarterly refunding (Wed Nov 4), Korea September current account (Thu Nov 5), US October payrolls (Fri Nov 6), Korea November 1–10 exports around Nov 11, then the BOK meeting on Nov 26; a KOSPI rebound with firm US data is the main risk to the long-end rally.
